<example>
<post>
Repair:
One tube.
Cutting it.
Separately, edible olive oil for cooking and inedible olive oil for a lamp.
</post>

<explanation>
"One tube" and "Cutting one tube" do not themselves establish repair; their repair-qualified subjects appear under every valid parent copy. Likewise, unqualified "Olive oil" includes both stated oils and cannot inherit edible or inedible quality. An edible oil is not necessarily for cooking, and an inedible oil is not necessarily for a lamp: those purposes remain in their qualified subjects. The stated combination of both oil uses remains a subject beneath every copy of each constituent; it does not replace either constituent.
</explanation>

edits.new:
<example>
<post>
Soup preparation:
One cup of water.
Heating it.
</post>

<explanation>
The list heading supplies soup-preparation purpose, and it refers to the listed water. But "Water" and "One cup of water" remain general headings: a cup of water for watering a plant also fits them. "Heating one cup of water" could instead be for an industrial process. Those headings cannot go beneath "Soup preparation". The complete source subject "Heating one cup of water for soup preparation" keeps both quantity and purpose, and appears beneath every copy of the qualified water, counted-water heating and soup-preparation heating headings.
</explanation>
